notes: §1985:VII.2.3.4 GR3: "The ASSIGN clause specifies the association of the file referenced by file-name-1 to a storage medium referenced by implementor-name-1 or literal-1." BindFileControl hands the TO phrase's operands to AssignTargetRule.Resolve, which returns the one operand that names the file (implementor-name-1's spelling or literal-1's value) into FileModel.AssignTarget; EmitFileRegistration emits it and FileRegistry.Register associates the file-name's connector with the host file CobolFile.ResolveHostPath maps it to. The members have no edition arm, so --std 85 reaches them as 2023 does; the 1985 arm is VisitAssignClause, which refuses the USING data-name-1 phrase 2023 adds (COBOL0900), leaving the two operands this rule names. Probed at 85: ASSIGN TO "ASGNFILE" writes asgnfile.txt, ASSIGN TO A1DEV writes a1dev.txt, ASSIGN DISK "a2file.dat" (no TO, a device class and a literal) writes a2file.dat, and each is read back; SPACES and a numeric literal are refused (COBOL2645, COBOL5506; §1985:VII.2.3.3 SR3), and ASSIGN USING is refused. One determination, not a divergence: a TO phrase of two file-naming operands is refused (COBOL2256) under the implementor's rule for the operands (§1985:VII.2.3.3 SR3: "The meaning and rules for the allowable content of implementor-name-1 and the value of literal-1 are defined by the implementor."; docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-71). The witness assigns a file to a literal, writes a record and reads it back.

next.reason: 1985: "to a storage medium referenced by implementor-name-1 or literal-1."; 2023: "to a physical file identified by device-name-1, literal-1, or the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1.". Same ASSIGN association subject. 2023 adds a case, the USING data-name-1 content, and fixes the association at OPEN, SORT or MERGE time. Device-name and literal association are unchanged.
